bigpic.b: Asia's chip rout deepened into the close
bigpic.t: with the Kospi down 6.2% to a January low as brokers questioned how long the AI memory boom can last.
with forecasts for headline PCE at 3.8%, while markets already fully price a quarter-point Fed hike on 9 December.

bigpic.b: Tariff and war risks keep Asia on edge
bigpic.t: as Washington readies Section 301 duties on 16 economies and tells Americans to leave Iran immediately.

stories.h: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
US Stocks Tumble On Hot Inflation, Trump Tariffs
Kospi closes down 6.2% at its lowest since January as Asia's chip rout deepens
stories.sum: The Kospi fell 6.16% to 4,697.51, its lowest close since 13 January, as foreign investors dumped a net 1.95 trillion won of shares. Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 2.8% to 57,011.62, Taiwan's Taiex about 5% and the Shanghai Composite 1.5% to its lowest in more than a year. Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.3%.
stories.why: Asian indices are packed with chip makers, so doubts about AI demand are now dragging on the whole region's markets.

stories.h: European shares open higher as luxury stocks offset a slide in chipmakers
stories.sum: The Stoxx 600 rose 0.5% to 636.01 in early trade on Wednesday, led by a 1.9% gain in personal and household goods. Swatch jumped 6%, Richemont 3% and Remy Cointreau 10.2% after setting targets to 2031/32, while technology shares fell 1.1% and Prosus 3.4% after a profit miss.
stories.why: Investors are rotating from AI hardware into consumer names, which could cushion Europe more than chip-heavy Asia.

stories.h: US PCE inflation, a GDP revision and the Beige Book land tonight before Thanksgiving
stories.sum: October PCE inflation and the revised third-quarter GDP figure are due at 8:30am ET, or 9:30pm in Singapore, with the Fed's Beige Book at 2pm ET. Forecasts compiled by Kotak Neo see headline PCE rising to 3.8% from 3.6% and core to 3.2% from 3.1%, with GDP growth revised up to 3.6% from 3.4%.
stories.why: A hot reading would cement a 9 Dec Fed hike, which markets already fully price, and pressure stretched tech valuations.

stories.h: Samsung and SK hynix plunge as brokers call an early peak in the memory boom
stories.sum: SK hynix fell 11.05% and Samsung Electronics 9.87%, pushing Samsung's value below 1,000 trillion won for the first time since March. BNP Paribas cut its Micron target to $775 from $1,700, and TrendForce trimmed its fourth-quarter NAND price forecast. Dell's operations chief said he still expects memory prices to rise.
stories.why: Memory makers have led the AI rally, so an earlier pricing downturn would hit earnings across the chip supply chain.

stories.h: Anthropic closes below its $83 IPO price after underwriters end price support
stories.sum: Anthropic shares fell 6.5% to about $81.90 on Tuesday, the first close below the $83 offer price, in its fourth session, after touching about $76. Lead underwriter Morgan Stanley exercised its full 147 million-share option and closed its stabilisation position after one day, Reuters reported. Buyers at the $111.50 opening are down about 26.5%.
stories.why: A weak start for the biggest AI listing could cool appetite for other AI IPOs and late-stage funding rounds.

stories.h: Dell raises its annual revenue forecast by $10B to $202B on AI server demand
stories.sum: Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $54.9B and adjusted EPS of $9.45 beat estimates of about $6.59. Dell booked $60.2B of AI orders, lifting its AI backlog to $132.3B, and added a $25B buyback. The shares, which fell 11.83% in Tuesday's session, rose about 3% to 4% after hours.
stories.why: Shows AI infrastructure orders still accelerating despite investor jitters over valuations and spending.

stories.h: FinCEN confirms intruders accessed some of its systems in a cyber incident
stories.sum: The US Treasury's financial crimes bureau said it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that gave unauthorised access to a limited subset of its systems, and has taken some offline as a precaution. Its BSA E-Filing site stays up. A 24 Nov order gives some filers until 30 December for reports due from 18 November, citing a service disruption.
stories.why: FinCEN holds sensitive bank reports on suspicious transactions, so a breach raises data-security and compliance worries across the industry.

stories.h: Bank of Korea expected to raise rates to 3.25% on Thursday despite the market rout
stories.sum: In a Seoul Economic Daily survey of 20 experts, 18 expect the central bank to lift its base rate by a quarter point from 3% on 26 Nov, and 14 see a peak of 3.5% in the first half of next year. The decision comes a day after the Kospi's 6.2% slump.
stories.why: A hike would widen Korean bank margins but add strain on indebted households and an already shaken stock market.

stories.h: Australia's inflation jumps to a three-year high of 4.9% as power bills surge
stories.sum: Annual CPI rose to 4.9% in October from 4.3% in September, above forecasts of about 4.8%, as electricity prices jumped 25.2% after government rebates expired. The trimmed mean measure climbed to 3.8% from 3.6%. Major bank economists still expect the Reserve Bank to hold at its final 2026 meeting on 7 to 8 December.
stories.why: Stubborn price pressures limit the RBA's room to ease, keeping borrowing costs high for Australian households and lenders.

stories.h: Bitcoin slips toward $59,000 as ETF outflows top $800M in two sessions
stories.sum: Bitcoin traded near $59,105 on Wednesday afternoon in Asia, down 2.2% in 24 hours, after US spot ETFs lost $569.7M on Monday and $231.6M on Tuesday, SoSoValue data show. Ether fell about 2.9% to $1,655. Traders are waiting for US PCE and GDP data due tonight.
stories.why: Steady ETF selling shows institutions are still cutting crypto exposure, removing a key source of demand.

stories.h: South Korea's draft crypto law would put banks in charge of won stablecoins
stories.sum: The Financial Services Commission unveiled a draft digital assets bill on 24 Nov that would initially limit won-pegged stablecoin issuance to consortia in which banks together hold a majority. Issuers would need at least 5 billion won of equity capital and FSC authorisation. The bill still has to pass the National Assembly.
stories.why: Bank-majority rules limit how far fintech and crypto firms can lead what could become a large won stablecoin market.

stories.h: CFTC lets futures markets count bitcoin, ether and stablecoins toward reserves
stories.sum: A 23 Nov staff advisory says swap venues, futures exchanges and clearing houses may count bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins toward the 12 months of operating costs they must hold, after valuation haircuts. The assets still do not qualify as cash or liquid securities for a separate liquidity test. The guidance is not a formal rule.
stories.why: Gives regulated derivatives firms a reason to hold crypto on their balance sheets, tying digital assets closer to US market plumbing.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price. It gains Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Insmed rose about 14% early, and Sanofi closed up 9.8% in Paris.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: Kymera hits a record high on oral eczema drug data and raises $1.75B
stories.sum: Kymera's once-daily pill KT-621 met all primary and secondary goals in a 16-week Phase 2 trial of 244 eczema patients. The company sold about 11.64 million shares at $150.37 to raise $1.75B, and Morgan Stanley lifted its target to $198 from $150. Gilead also hit a record after William Blair started coverage at outperform.
stories.why: An effective pill could challenge injected eczema treatments such as Sanofi's Dupixent, raising the stakes for big immunology franchises.

stories.h: GSK's twice-yearly Exdensur matches monthly Nucala in a rare vasculitis trial
stories.sum: In the Phase 3 OCEAN trial of 162 patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, depemokimab given every 26 weeks was non-inferior to mepolizumab every four weeks on remission over 52 weeks, with similar side effects. GSK plans to file for approval in the first half of 2027.
stories.why: Fewer injections could help GSK move patients from its older Nucala to longer-acting Exdensur before rivals arrive.

stories.h: Oil Jumps Over 2% as Saudi Arabia Downs Drones Over Ras Tanura
US tells Americans to leave Iran immediately, warning hostilities could escalate
stories.sum: A security alert from the US Virtual Embassy in Iran told citizens not to travel there for any reason and to leave at once, warning that Iran, the Houthis and allied groups may target US companies and institutions. It follows Iranian attacks on US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait and a Houthi strike that wounded 11 people in Riyadh.
stories.why: An evacuation call signals Washington is bracing for escalation that could threaten Gulf energy sites and tanker routes.

stories.h: Oil and European gas fall as surplus fears outweigh new Hormuz attacks
stories.sum: Brent fell 1.73% to $89.82 a barrel and WTI 1.77% to $80.60 by 0745 GMT, while Dutch TTF gas dropped 3.9% to 88.10 euros per MWh. UKMTO said three ships crossing Hormuz were hit by projectiles. The IEA expects a fourth-quarter surplus, and EU gas storage sits below 69% against an 86% seasonal norm.
stories.why: Thin European gas stocks heading into winter leave prices exposed if Gulf disruption worsens, even with oil supply ample.

stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 baselines as Iraq rejects the capacity review
stories.sum: The 29 Nov ministerial meeting is expected to set a 2027 framework based on a commissioned assessment of members' capacity, since group-wide targets end on 31 Dec. Iraq has rejected that assessment, setting up a possible clash. Seven core members hold combined targets at 31.01M barrels a day.
stories.why: New baselines decide who can pump more next year as the market tips toward surplus.

stories.h: BYD enters exclusive talks to buy Ineos' Hambach car plant in France
stories.sum: BYD said it is in exclusive negotiations to buy the Hambach factory in Moselle, near the German border, which Ineos Automotive has owned since 2020 and uses to build its Grenadier 4x4. The deal depends on consultation with staff representatives. President Macron and Industry Minister Sebastien Martin welcomed the plan.
stories.why: Building cars inside the EU would cut BYD's exposure to tariffs on China-made EVs and speed its push into Europe.

stories.h: Li Auto halves its quarterly loss and returns to positive free cash flow
stories.sum: Third-quarter revenue rose 5.4% to 28.8B yuan ($4.3B) on 99,964 deliveries, up 7.2%, and the net loss narrowed 50.4% to 309.7M yuan. Vehicle margin recovered to 15.3% from 9.4% in the second quarter, and free cash flow reached 2.0B yuan. Li Auto expects 110,000 to 115,000 deliveries in the fourth quarter.
stories.why: Margin repair at Li Auto shows some Chinese EV makers can steady profits despite the sector's price war.

stories.h: Tesla and SpaceX name five directors to steer possible merger talks, FT reports
stories.sum: Tesla directors Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung and SpaceX's Roelof Botha and Randy Glein will guide special committees weighing an all-stock combination, the FT reported on 24 Nov. Evercore advises Tesla, and Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs advise SpaceX. Neither company commented; Bloomberg has said a deal could come as soon as December.
stories.why: A merger would tie Tesla's car business to Musk's rocket and satellite empire, changing how investors value the EV maker.

stories.h: Black Friday discounts run shallower than last year as retailers guard margins
stories.sum: Centric data cited by LSEG show the average US online discount at 30% this month, down from 33% in Black Friday week 2025, even as 38% of products are on sale against a 35% average last year. Specialty retailers' discounts shrank to 23% from 31%. LSEG expects fourth-quarter retail and restaurant earnings to rise 8.5% on 3.5% revenue growth.
stories.why: Shallower markdowns protect profits but test shoppers already stretched by inflation running at 3.7%.

stories.h: Abercrombie, Kohl's and Dick's rally after beating forecasts before Black Friday
stories.sum: Abercrombie & Fitch jumped 20% after record third-quarter sales of $1.44B, up 11%, with comparable sales up 6%. Kohl's surged by double digits as comparable sales grew 1.2% and it raised its outlook, while Dick's lifted its adjusted EPS guidance to $11.45 to $12.30. Tariff refunds flattered several results.
stories.why: Strong reports into the holiday weekend suggest shoppers are still spending, though partly on higher prices.

stories.h: Best Buy raises its outlook after its strongest comparable sales in five years
stories.sum: Comparable sales rose 6.1% in the third quarter and revenue reached $10.24B, against $9.67B a year earlier. Adjusted EPS was $1.62. Best Buy lifted its full-year revenue forecast to $43.0B to $43.3B and comparable sales to 3.4% to 4.0%. Bespoke notes PC prices rose about 25% on memory costs while unit sales fell.
stories.why: Shoppers are absorbing electronics price rises driven by the AI memory squeeze, lifting sales in dollars rather than units.

stories.h: Hexed and Focker In-Law open today, with Hunger Games tipped to win Thanksgiving
stories.sum: Variety's projections put Disney's Hexed, which cost more than $200M to make, and Universal's Focker In-Law at $40M to $45M each over the five-day holiday. Lionsgate's Sunrise on the Reaping, which opened to $120M, is tracking for $80M to $90M. Domestic ticket sales are running 20% ahead of 2025.
stories.why: Thanksgiving is a key test of whether cinemas' 2026 recovery can carry into the year-end season.

stories.h: Netflix buys Los Angeles' Radford Studio Center for $380M
stories.sum: Netflix bought the 55-acre Studio City lot, which has 22 stages, directly from Goldman Sachs-led lenders who took it from Hackman Capital Partners, which paid $1.85B in 2021. The streamer plans renovations and will keep the studio team, calling the purchase a meaningful new investment in California's film industry.
stories.why: Distressed studio lots are changing hands far below peak prices, letting streamers lock in production space cheaply.

stories.h: Skydance merges Warner Bros. TV and Paramount TV studios into one unit
stories.sum: The combined Warner Bros. Television Studios, launching in early 2027, will pool more than 120 franchises including The Pitt and Ted Lasso. Former Netflix executives Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell will run it as co-presidents under George Cheeks. CBS Studios stays separate, and further layoffs are possible.
stories.why: Hollywood consolidation is shrinking the number of major studio buyers, squeezing writers, producers and suppliers.

stories.h: US Air Force orders 15 more Boeing KC-46 tankers for $2.82B
stories.sum: The contract change, awarded on 24 Nov for Lot 13, completes the initial 188-jet US tranche and lifts total KC-46A orders worldwide to 203. The tankers will be built in Seattle, with work due by June 2030. At about $188M each including services, Lot 13 costs more per jet than Lot 12's $165M.
stories.why: Steady tanker orders give Boeing's defence arm a long production runway as the Air Force replaces ageing KC-135s.

stories.h: Airbus needs about 200 more deliveries in five weeks to hit its 2026 goal
stories.sum: Airbus delivered 621 jets through October, up 6.2% on a year earlier, and 46 more in November through Monday, Cirium data show, leaving about 203 to reach its 870 target. Analysts expect 90 to 100 in November and 150 to 160 in December. A new EASA directive orders repeat checks on A350 horizontal stabiliser fasteners.
stories.why: A miss would raise fresh doubts about Airbus's supply chain recovery and its plans to lift output.

stories.h: Malaysia Airlines orders 10 Boeing 787s to replace its A350s from 2032
stories.sum: Malaysia Aviation Group signed for 10 787 Dreamliners with options for six more at a Kuala Lumpur ceremony attended by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Deliveries run from 2032 to 2035, gradually replacing its seven A350s. The GEnx-powered jets will seat 319 in three classes on routes such as London, Sydney and Tokyo. No value was disclosed.
stories.why: Another Asian widebody win for Boeing, though 2030s delivery dates show how long airlines must wait for new jets.

stories.h: US home price growth slows to its weakest pace since May, Redfin says
stories.sum: Redfin's index rose 0.14% in October, the smallest monthly gain in six months, and 3.5% from a year earlier, the slowest annual rise since May. Prices fell in 20 of 50 metros, led by Seattle at 1.2% on the month, while San Francisco led annual gains at 12.7%.
stories.why: Cooling prices and high mortgage rates erode owners' equity gains and point to a slower 2027 for builders and lenders.

stories.h: Homes.com sees US home sales falling 5.6% in 2027 with prices flat
stories.sum: Its 2027 outlook for 40 large markets forecasts national sales down 5.6% and prices up just 0.04%, with declines in 24 of the 40 markets. Seattle prices are seen falling 2.4% as supply rises 4.9%. The forecast lands with Freddie Mac's 30-year rate at 7.28% and a Fed hike expected in December.
stories.why: Another weak year would squeeze brokers, mortgage lenders and builders already coping with decade-low sales.

stories.h: Mortgage rates at 7.28% push existing-home sales to a decade low
stories.sum: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed rate reached 7.28% in the survey released 19 November, up from 7.11% a week earlier, with the next reading brought forward to Wednesday by the holiday. The National Association of Realtors said October existing-home sales ran at an annual 3.75 million, the weakest pace since 2010.
stories.why: Borrowing costs at their highest since 2000 are freezing out buyers and squeezing agents, builders and lenders.

stories.h: Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies, including Singapore and Malaysia, look imminent
stories.sum: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to announce duties on 16 economies found to have built excess industrial capacity, with Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia among those likely hit, logistics firm Dimerco says. Rates and timing are not yet public, steel and aluminum are excluded, and Taiwan expects its rate to stay at an agreed 15% cap.
stories.why: New duties would hit the region's export-driven electronics makers just as AI-related trade is lifting growth.

stories.h: Malaysian car discounts reach 15% as a price war squeezes carmakers, CIMB says
stories.sum: CIMB Securities says Toyota and Honda are offering discounts of 3% to 15% of list prices, while Perodua has rebates of RM1,500 to RM7,500 on some models for November and December. It forecasts 2026 industry volume up 2.2% to 815,000 units, above the Malaysian Automotive Association's 800,000, and keeps a neutral call on the sector.
stories.why: Heavy discounting lifts volumes but erodes margins for Malaysian carmakers and dealers heading into 2027.

stories.h: Singapore core inflation eases to 1.5% in October on cheaper electricity
stories.sum: Core inflation slowed to 1.5% from 2% in September and headline inflation to 1.9%, as a lower regulated electricity tariff cut energy inflation to 1% from 8.7%. MAS and the trade ministry expect core inflation of 1.5% to 2% this year and 1.5% to 2.5% in 2027, with a pickup in the first quarter.
stories.why: Easing price pressure gives MAS room to keep policy steady even as growth runs hot on AI exports.
